title: Mar Shmuel Mar

paragraphs: He lived in the time of Rava and Rav Papa; see [Beitzah 21b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.21b.11): Rava asked Mar Shmuel to expound publicly. Hyman reports that Dikdukei Soferim adds a second “Mar.”[^12]
Similarly [Niddah 66a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.66a.19): Rava had Rav Shmuel expound publicly. Hyman reads “Mar” in place of “Rav.”

And [Beitzah 14b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.14b.2-3): Rav Pappi happened to come to the house of Mar Shmuel [Mar, per Dikdukei Soferim]; porridge was brought to him and he did not eat, because of the servants’ disregard for the rules. Hyman infers from this that he was very wealthy, and it is possible, as the Yuchasin holds, that he was the Exilarch or from the house of the Exilarch. In Toldot Yisrael by the scholar designated הר״ח יעב״ץ, vol. 6, p. 54, note 2, he says this refers to Shmuel, the colleague of Rav; Hyman replies: with all due respect, this is a mistake.
And in [Menachot 34a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.34a.5) (35a in Hyman’s citation): Rav Papa happened to come to the house of Mar Shmuel, saw a certain opening, etc.

And [Beitzah 25b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.25b.11): Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: I brought Mar Shmuel out from the sun into the shade, etc. But Hyman reports a reading in Dikdukei Soferim in which Rav Shemen bar Abba said so: I brought Mar Shmuel out, and Hyman identifies this as Shmuel, the colleague of Rav, who was the teacher of Rav Shemen bar Abba, as in Ketubot 106b. So too what the Sefer HaDorot cites under the entry Mar Shmuel from [Eruvin 102a:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.102a.12), that certain mortar that was in the house of Mar Shmuel; from Bava Metzia 15b in Hyman’s citation (compare [Bava Metzia 16b:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.16b.9)), that Rabbi Yaakov, father of Rav Nachman, was his scribe; from [Niddah 25b:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.25b.9), that certain gestational sac that was brought before Mar Shmuel; and likewise [Berakhot 19a:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.19a.3), that one spoke after Mar Shmuel:[^13] Hyman argues that in all of these the Sefer HaDorot erred, for they refer to Shmuel, the colleague of Rav, who was always called by the name Mar Shmuel, both in his presence and not in his presence, as explained in his entry.[^14]

Hyman writes that Mar Shmuel Mar had a son, citing [Nedarim 55a](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.55a.5): the son of Mar Shmuel directed that twelve thousand zuz [supplied יב׳; the checked William Davidson text has thirteen thousand] be given to Rava; and Hyman suggests that possibly it should read Mar Shmuel and the word 'bar' is superfluous.

notes.text: Hyman prints 'ר״פ'; rendered Rav Papa by contextual reading, as Rav Papa is named in the same entry. The printed abbreviation is preserved here as uncertain.

'דק״ס' rendered Dikdukei Soferim, 'סה״ד' as Sefer HaDorot, and 'היוחסין' as the Yuchasin, by conventional expansion; these are not verified against a supplied witness. 'ר״נ' in 'ר״נ בר יצחק' rendered Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak as printed 'אר״נ'.

The source prints 'להר״ח יעב״ץ' (Rabbi Chaim Yaavetz) with 'בח״ו צד 54 בהערה 2' kept as printed; modern numbering not supplied. The OCR gave 'ח״ז' and 'הערה 9'; the proofread text reads 'ח״ו' and 'הערה 2'.

Bracketed text [מר, דק״ס] and [צ״ל למר] are Hyman's textual variants and emendation, kept as printed; 'צ״ל' means 'it should read'. Hyman's final suggestion that 'בר' is superfluous is his own conjecture.
Printed 'ב״א' in 'רב שמן ב״א' read as bar Abba, following the full name given earlier in the same unit; 'מב״מ' read as Bava Metzia by conventional expansion.

The bound Davidson Nedarim55a paragraph reads תליסר אלפי, thirteen thousand; Hyman’s supplied יב׳ is twelve. Both readings are displayed, not harmonized. פקיד denotes an instruction to pay Rava, not a deposit with Rava. Hyman’s possible deletion of בר does not establish either a new son or the identity of the speaker; the root hold remains.

The checked Beitzah 21b paragraph has Mar Shmuel and Niddah 66a has Rav Shmuel; Hyman’s “it should read Mar” is retained as his proposed correction. The servants wording in Beitzah 14b is explained here in the context of pounding-food restrictions, following nearby Rashi comments about servants disregarding the rules. The named doorway passage was positively read at Menachot 34a beside the supplied 35a; Bava Metzia 16b names Rav Nachman’s father among Mar Shmuel’s judicial scribes but does not name him Yaakov, beside Hyman’s supplied 15b and Yaakov. Beitzah 25b has Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak bringing Mar Shmuel between sun and shade. The reported Dikdukei Soferim alternative, Yuchasin and Toldot Yisrael identifications, and teacher reference at Ketubot 106b have not been independently established here. Hyman’s separation of the two Shmuels, criticism of Seder HaDorot, wealth inference, and possible deletion of bar remain his account; no identity, genealogy or chronology is admitted. The historical note’s given-name expansion and printed/OCR comparison are preserved as inherited claims, not fresh printed-source verification.

Dikdukei Soferim on Beitzah records more than one name form. At 14b (p. 29, note ט) the apparatus reports Mar Shmuel, Shmuel Mar and Mar Shmuel Mar in different witnesses. At 21b (p. 50, note פ) the manuscript column adds a second “Mar.” At 25b (p. 64, note ש) the manuscript column has Shimon bar Abba where the printed text has Nachman bar Yitzchak. The note also records Rav Shemen bar Abba, the form Hyman cites. The apparatus discusses different historical identifications as possibilities.

The consulted Seder HaDorot entry “Mar Shmuel Mari” groups the mortar, gestational sac, scribe, shade and doorway episodes under one heading. Its portrayal of him as a possible Exilarch and Hyman’s separation of the various episodes are the respective authors’ accounts. The consulted Bava Metzia 16b calls Rav Nachman’s father one of Mar Shmuel’s court scribes and leaves him unnamed in the passage. The exact Toldot Yisrael page and the original Yuchasin passage have not been independently collated.

Hyman’s printed text (vol. III, pp. 1149–1150) gives twelve thousand and treats deletion of bar as a possibility. In the consulted Nedarim 55a, the son of Mar Shmuel directs payment of thirteen thousand zuz to Rava from the proceeds at Nehar Panya, prompting a discussion about what those proceeds include. The consulted Seder HaDorot notice also gives thirteen thousand. Hyman’s conjecture leaves open who gave the instruction.

[Beitzah 21b:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.21b.11) reads Mar Shmuel, while [Niddah 66a:19](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.66a.19) reads Rav Shmuel. [Beitzah 14b:2–3](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.14b.2-3) gives the servants’ disregard for the rules as one explanation. [Seder HaDorot 3370](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3370&lang=en) associates the Beitzah reports and the instruction by the son of Mar Shmuel in [Nedarim 55a:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.55a.5) with this entry. Hyman assigns some of Heilprin’s other citations to Shmuel, Rav’s colleague, and proposes a different reading of the name in [Beitzah 25b:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.25b.11).

The four linked passages give Mar Shmuel. In Bava Metzia, Rav Nachman calls his father one of the scribes of Mar Shmuel’s judges and leaves his father unnamed. Hyman calls him Yaakov and cites 15b. In Berakhot the person speaks after Mar Shmuel’s death, as the context makes clear.

In [Ketubot 107b:10-11](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.107b.10-11), Rav Shemen bar Abba reports Shmuel’s interpretation of the maintenance case. The first version calls Shmuel “our teacher in Babylonia.” Hyman cites Ketubot 106b. This report concerns the cited teaching relationship, independently of the name variant in Beitzah.
